```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library("naboer")
available <- requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("units", quietly = TRUE)
```

Use `sf` geometry columns and physical distance units. Projected queries use
indexed candidates with exact geometry-to-geometry distance checks. Geographic
queries respect the current sf spherical/ellipsoidal engine. Constructors never
change `sf_use_s2()`, repair invalid geometry or assume a missing CRS.

```{r spatial, eval=available}
sites <- sf::st_as_sf(
  tibble::tibble(site = letters[1:6], east = c(0, 100, 500, 1000, 2000, 3000), north = 0),
  coords = c("east", "north"), crs = 32632
)
f <- neighbourhoods(sites, spatial = spatial_window(units::set_units(200, "m")))
tibble::as_tibble(f, folds = 1:3, membership = TRUE)
```

Square and hexagonal block widths are distinct from buffers. Custom polygon
regions are also supported. A shared boundary belongs to the first region in
deterministic region order. Overlapping region interiors require an explicit
integer `assignment` column. Non-point observations retain their original
geometry; block assignment uses the first intersecting block rather than
silently substituting a centroid.

```{r blocks, eval=available}
blocks <- spatial_folds(sites, size = units::set_units(500, "m"))
buffered <- buffer_folds(blocks, spatial = spatial_window(units::set_units(100, "m")))
tibble::as_tibble(buffered)
```

Generated geographic grids use a local azimuthal equidistant projection. For
large extents, select an appropriate explicit projected `grid_crs`. Physical
distance radii remain separate from that grid representation.

## Repeated station observations

```{r joint, eval=available}
observations <- sites[rep(seq_len(nrow(sites)), each = 10), ]
observations$date <- rep(as.Date("2024-01-01") + 0:9, nrow(sites))
joint <- neighbourhoods(
  observations,
  key = site, index = date,
  spatial = spatial_window(units::set_units(200, "m")),
  temporal = temporal_window(time_span(1, "days")),
  combine = "intersection"
)
tibble::as_tibble(joint, folds = c(1, 15, 60))
```

Intersection omits observations close in both space and time. Union omits
observations close in either dimension. These represent different assumptions
about residual dependence. `.by` imposes hard independent-domain boundaries in
either case; keys identify stations and need not imply independent residuals.
For fixed stations, geometry relationships are reused across times. Moving
locations use each observation's geometry.

## Cubble

Both nested spatial and long temporal cubbles are accepted. `fold_data()` gives
one canonical row per temporal observation. Its `naboer_source` attribute maps
canonical rows back to the nested spatial row and within-series row, or to the
source long row. Actual spatial `sf` geometries are restored for temporal
cubbles; polygon geometry is preserved.

```{r cubble, eval=available && requireNamespace("cubble", quietly=TRUE)}
values <- tibble::tibble(
  site = rep(letters[1:6], each = 10),
  date = rep(as.Date("2024-01-01") + 0:9, 6), value = seq_len(60)
)
cube <- cubble::make_cubble(spatial = sites, temporal = values, key = site, index = date)
cube_folds <- neighbourhoods(cube,
  spatial = spatial_window(units::set_units(200, "m")),
  temporal = temporal_window(time_span(1, "days")), combine = "intersection"
)
head(fold_data(cube_folds))
```

Use `spatiotemporal_folds(mode = "crossed")` for joint block holdouts,
`mode = "space"` for holding locations out across all times, and `mode = "time"`
for holding periods out across stations.
